data.name: Dottore
data.description:
He never came off as malicious, but an utter lack of compassion permeated throughout our conversation. From his tone, I can sense that he's always looked down on others.

—Tighnari about his confrontation with Dottore, As by a God's Side
While he was a scholar at Sumeru Akademiya, Zandik had a fascination with the Khaenri'ahn machines found in Devantaka Mountain and the ancient desert city of Gurabad. This interest was scorned and even deemed dangerous by his peers and teachers, and he ended up taking drastic measures to ensure the secrecy of his work.

From Zandik's own writing, his passion for uncovering the secrets behind ancient technology is clear. Despite being at odds with most of his peers and being described as "rigid" in his thinking by Sohreh, he was apparently a fairly good conversationalist and managed to strike a fast friendship with the senior Dastur despite her initial doubts.[8] However, it is possible that Zandik had actually done this to lure her away and murder her, thus ensuring her silence about what he had been up to inside the jungle. He was also a quick thinker, as he apparently saved his team from a highly dangerous machine.[9]

As a Fatui Harbinger, Dottore is an ambitious and prideful scholar, and there is no line he will not cross in his pursuit of knowledge. His primary goal is to prove that ordinary humans can be modified to become equals with the gods, yet he seems to hold little regard for human life. In his quest to further bolster humanity's combat abilities, he has researched Khaenri'ah's Automatons; researched ways to weaponize The Withering and Eleazar; and sought to utilize the power of dreams to elevate humanity's cognitive abilities. In the manga, a young segment of his kills his subordinate Krupp for disloyalty only to temporarily forget the entire affair in a short span of time,[10] and later transforms Krupp's corpse into an autonomous Ruin Hunter-like machine for no known reason besides his own amusement.

Despite holding gods and Vision-bearers in great disdain, he has a tense but peaceful talk with Tighnari and in his second confrontation with Lesser Lord Kusanali, claims that he wants to show her "proper respect and dignity." However, both of his conversation partners remark that he only acts that way because of his absolute confidence in himself, not out of true respect.[11] He is delighted by Lesser Lord Kusanali's disapproval of his usage of segments and expresses his disappointment that the God of Wisdom is bound by conventional rules of logic. However, he underestimates her and is taken by surprise when she successfully coerces him into destroying his segments in exchange for the Electro Gnosis.[12]

To surpass the limits of his own human cognition, Dottore created segments of himself using different points of his life as a basis. Accordingly, each segment has its own personality, and the segments are not necessarily in accord. Dottore acknowledges that he has "long grown tired of their doubts and endless arguments" during his second confrontation with Lesser Lord Kusanali, and tells her that her plan only worked because "this segment [she sees] now is the most selfish." The other segments also express their shock and rage to him as they are erased, with one calling his decision "short-sighted" while another futilely begs for him to wait.[12] A Fatui sergeant, who is unaware of the existence of segments, comments on the stark differences between the Dottore in search of Haypasia, whom he finds more smiling, and the version he met in Snezhnaya.[11]

Despite these character differences, his different versions of himself are not without commonalities. Although it seems quieter than the segment featured in the manga, the first Omega Build segment seen in the Sumeru Archon Quests displays thus the same sadistic streak. He does not, for example, hesitate to endanger the lives of others for his own purposes, such as when he manipulates the minds of innocent civilians to corner the Traveler and Lesser Lord Kusanali in their initial confrontation.[7] This personality trait also appears to be present in some, if not all, of his other segments: the second Dottore whom the Traveler meets in Sumeru, seeking to kidnap Haypasia, gives Tighnari a veiled threat after the former refuses to acquiesce to the Doctor's demands, and cheerfully waves goodbye to Dehya and the Traveler when he sees that he successfully lured them away from Haypasia.

In the manga, Dottore displays manic tendencies, laughing maniacally or making unintelligible noises to himself when he is in a good mood, but also being highly irritable whenever he does not immediately get his way.
